question.text: Syndicate ABC LLP committed INR 25 crore (lead Mr. A: INR 5 cr; other accredited LPs: INR 20 cr) with 15% carry to the lead. Exit is INR 75 crore after 3 years. After computing the lead's carry (INR 7.50 crore on INR 50 crore profit), the REMAINING distribution of INR 67.50 crore is split pro-rata based on committed capital. How much does Mr. A receive in TOTAL (his carry + his pro-rata share as an LP)?

answer.text: INR 21.00 crore (carry INR 7.50 cr + pro-rata INR 13.50 cr)
INR 13.50 crore (pro-rata only, including his INR 5 cr)

explanation.text: The Logic: Step 1: Exit INR 75 cr, committed capital INR 25 cr, profit = INR 50 cr. Carry to lead = 15% × INR 50 cr = INR 7.50 cr. Step 2: Remaining = INR 75 − 7.50 = INR 67.50 cr to be distributed pro-rata. Mr. A's pro-rata = (5/25) × 67.50 = INR 13.50 cr. Step 3: Mr. A's total = 7.50 (carry) + 13.50 (pro-rata) = INR 21.00 crore. Per Ch 11.1.2 syndicate mechanics. The Trap: Option A counts only the carry, ignoring Mr. A's own LP participation. Option B counts only pro-rata, ignoring his lead carry. Option D gives him the entire pool, which is wrong. Cross-Exam Context: Carry + co-investor distribution math tested in XIX-A and XIX-C waterfall/syndicate scenarios. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always model the lead's blended return — if carry + pro-rata lifts their IRR above a 'reasonable manager's' level, LPs challenge the carry percentage. 15% is market-standard; anything higher needs serious justification.
